# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. NUMBER PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Fill cells with numbers according to constraints*

### 1.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraint
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 block
- **Hitori** — Eliminate duplicates in rows/columns by blacking out cells

### 1.2 Region-Based Number Filling
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbered blocks matching their size
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with 1–N; duplicates must be separated by their value
- **Makaro** — Fill rooms with 1–N; arrows indicate which neighbor holds the maximum

### 1.3 Cross-Referenced / Positional Numbers
- **Nansuke** — Fill grid with multi-digit numbers from a given list

---

## 2. REGION DIVISION PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Partition the grid into valid regions*

### 2.1 Division into Uniform Rectangles or Squares
- **Shikaku** — Divide into rectangles each containing exactly one number equal to its area
- **Choco Banana** — Black rectangles/squares; white regions may not be rectangular

### 2.2 Division into Polyomino Shapes
- **Five Cells** — Divide into pentominoes; numbers indicate boundary line count
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped (one-cell-wide) blocks
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing matching white and gray sub-regions
- **Evolomino** — Divide into blocks that evolve in shape along arrow sequences

### 2.3 Division with Color/Shade Constraints
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per region; same-shape tetrominoes cannot touch
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of black cells) with exactly two per bold-line region
- **Nuritwin** — Each region contains two same-size shaded blocks; all shading connected
- **Sto-stone** — Color cells in rooms; when "dropped," they fill the bottom half exactly

---

## 3. CELL SHADING / PAINTING PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

### 3.1 Shading with Connectivity and Adjacency Rules
- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form a connected wall; white "islands" match given numbers
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells in rooms; no two shaded cells adjacent, white cells connected
- **Kurodoko** — Shade cells; numbered cells count visible white cells in four directions
- **Kurotto** — Shade cells; circles indicate sum of connected black-cell groups adjacent to them
- **Usowan** — Shade cells; each bold-line region has exactly one incorrect number clue

### 3.2 Shading with Structural Shape Rules
- **Choco Banana** *(also §2.1)* — Black groups must be rectangular; white groups must not be
- **Shakashaka** — Place right triangles in cells; remaining white space must form rectangles
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire tiles; diagonal-number clues constrain row/column black-cell counts

### 3.3 Shading with Path / Maze Constraints
- **Nurimeizu** — Paint cells to create a maze from S to G; circle cells on shortest path, triangles off it
- **Nurimisaki** — Paint cells; circled "promontory" cells have exactly one white neighbor

---

## 4. LOOP / PATH DRAWING PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Draw a single continuous closed loop*

### 4.1 Unconstrained Loop with Circle/Marker Rules
- **Masyu** — Loop must turn at black circles and go straight at white circles (with turns adjacent)
- **Slitherlink** — Connect dots to form a loop; numbers indicate how many sides of each cell are used
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through each black circle at the circle's midpoint

### 4.2 Loop with Regional Alternation Rules
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Within each bold-line region, loop either turns at all white circles or goes straight through all
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through moon or sun cells (not both) per room, alternating type each room

### 4.3 Loop with Directional / Wind Constraints
- **Nagareru** — Directional loop; wind arrows constrain which direction the loop may travel
- **Suraromu** — Loop passes through numbered "gates" in a specific order; starts/ends at a numbered circle

### 4.4 Loop with Black-Cell Avoidance
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells; arrow-number clues indicate black cell counts in a direction

---

## 5. CONNECTION / BRIDGE PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Connect elements by drawing lines or bridges*

### 5.1 Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (1–2 per pair); all islands linked

### 5.2 Path / Flow Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-overlapping paths

---

## 6. OBJECT PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Place objects (lights, numbers, symbols) in cells*

### 6.1 Light / Visibility Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs so every white cell is illuminated; numbered cells constrain adjacent bulbs

### 6.2 Snake / Sequence Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot touch or "see" one another

### 6.3 Symbol Fill (Non-numeric)
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; territories constrain the imbalance between the two symbols

---

## 7. MOVEMENT / MIGRATION PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Move existing objects to valid target positions*

### 7.1 Circle/Piece Migration
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into their home country; numbered circles travel an exact distance
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; gray area numbers must match sum of entering circles

---

## 8. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC PUZZLES
*Combine two or more of the above primary mechanics*

### 8.1 Shading + Number Placement
- **Chained Block** — Black cell groups form "blocks"; blocks chain at corners; each chain has unique shapes

### 8.2 Region Division + Number Placement
- **Sto-stone** *(also §2.3)* — Room division combined with gravity-based drop constraint

### 8.3 Path Drawing + Shading
- **Nurimeizu** *(also §3.3)* — Shading creates the maze; path validity drives shading decisions

### 8.4 Object Placement + Sequential Constraint
- **Evolomino** *(also §2.2)* — Block shapes must grow sequentially along an arrow without rotation/flip
- **Pencils** — Mark out pencil shapes; lines from tips traverse cells up to a numbered length

### 8.5 Movement + Connectivity
- **Satogaeri** *(also §7.1)* — Migration constrained by non-crossing tracks and country boundaries

---
